result: The previous finding is closed. I found no blocking issue, and the range need not hold the push on security grounds. The built-in `/security-review` could not run: its preprocessing failed with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/HEAD...'`, because the checkout has no `origin/HEAD`. findings:
- Previous finding closed. `scope.ts:208-235` now lists the whole index with `git ls-files --cached -z`. It compares every distinct top-level component, other than the literal `.claude`, with the `.claude` folder by `lstat` dev and ino.
  - A committed `.claude.`, `.claude ` (trailing space), a name with an HFS+ ignorable code point, or a `CLAUDE~1` short name is a top-level component. Each resolves to the folder's identity on a folding file system. `repositoryControl` then returns a reason (`scope.ts:232-233`), so `installedScope` (`scope.ts:269-277`) keeps `user`.
- Skip of the literal `.claude` (`scope.ts:230`): safe. Any index entry under the literal `.claude` is already handled. `scope.ts:217-218` catches the file, the folder or a gitlink, `scope.ts:219-224` catches identity aliases under the prefix, and `scope.ts:175` returns early if `.claude` is a symlink.
- Lowercase prefix filter (`scope.ts:211-215`): safe. Only `.claude`'s ASCII letters matter, and none has a non-ASCII `toLowerCase` collision. Any folding beyond case is caught by the component loop, not the filter.
- Nested aliases: none open. An alias of the root-level `.claude` has to be a top-level name. A symlinked component gives its own `lstat` identity, but git writes no entry through it (it replaces the link with a real directory), so it cannot make the file repository-controlled.
- Low, non-blocking (hardening, requires a git bug or a hand-crafted index):
  - `scope.ts:221` runs the file-identity check only on prefix-filtered entries. A tracked `link/settings.local.json`, where `link` is a symlink to `.claude` and git wrote through it, would be missed.
  - Fix: run the file-identity check over `everything`, or note the limit in the JSDoc.
- Cost (non-blocking):
  - `git ls-files` output is unbounded in memory (`shell.ts:113-123`).
  - The `lstat` calls run sequentially, one per distinct top-level name, so a repository with very many top-level names slows setup.
  - This runs only when the local file enables the plugin in a trusted work tree. A Shell failure returns exit 127, so the code fails closed (`scope.ts:209`).
- Fail-closed: a file system that reports ino 0 can make two entries compare equal, which gives a false match and so `user` scope. It cannot give a false untracked.

verdict: previous finding closed; no blocker; do not hold the push.
